Kaplan Legacy

One family. Seventy years. Twenty-five thousand front doors.

1952

Nathan Kaplan builds the first house.

A single-family home in Lakewood, New Jersey — the first of what would become a company built on the idea that a house should be built the way you'd build one for your own family.

1960s–1990s

Michael & Morris Kaplan take the reins.

The second generation expands Kaplan beyond New Jersey into Pennsylvania, Texas, Florida and Georgia, diversifying into retail development and modular building. In 1989, the NAHB names Kaplan the nation's most diversified builder.

2005

Jason Kaplan becomes president.

The third generation takes over as the company shifts its focus toward rental communities and urban redevelopment — meeting a new generation of residents where they actually want to live.

Today

14 communities. 3,675 units. 11 cities.

Still family-run. Still building the kind of neighborhoods a Kaplan would want to come home to.

New Homes & Commercial

Beyond rentals: building what a neighborhood actually needs.

Kaplan's roots are in home construction — and the company still develops new residential and commercial projects alongside its rental portfolio.

New Homes

Ground-up residential development, built with the same standards Nathan Kaplan set in 1952.

Commercial

Retail and mixed-use development that anchors the neighborhoods Kaplan builds around.
